title: Augmented two-term resolution of finite coefficients over completed coefficients
statement: Fix universes d,t,u, a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a scheme Y in universe t, a finite-field datum D in universe d with characteristic unequal to l, and n a natural number. Put R equal to the completed integral coefficient ring sheaf on the pro-etale site of Y. The restriction to R of the finite coefficient unit at level n, placed in degree zero, admits an augmented resolution Q. The complex Q is K-flat, is zero outside degrees -1 and 0, and its terms in these degrees are isomorphic to the R-module unit. The augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The restriction functor and coefficient objects are exactly those of [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models] and [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].

proof.text: Use PrincipalKoszulStrictReplacement.completed_exact for the actual completed coefficient ring, the recorded uniformizer power and the actual quotient projection. This gives a short exact sequence from the unit to the unit to the finite coefficient unit with scalars restricted along the limit projection. The finite-field datum is irrelevant to the construction of the completed ring.

Apply the degree-zero single functor to this short exact sequence and take the mapping cone of its first arrow. The cone term in degree i is U[0]^(i+1) direct sum U[0]^i. The zero-summand biproduct isomorphisms identify its terms in degrees -1 and 0 with the unit; all other terms vanish. These are Mathlib homotopyCofiber.XIsoBiprod, isoBiprodZero, isoZeroBiprod and singleObjXSelf.

The unit is categorically flat. Transport this property along the two coordinate isomorphisms; all other terms are flat because they are zero. The site-sheaf tensor comparison gives IsFlatOnSite for every term. The support calculation gives the upper bound zero, so the independent-coefficient bounded-flat criterion makes the constructed complex K-flat.

The single functor is exact. Mathlib mappingCone.descShortComplex gives the augmentation of its short exact image, and mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex makes this augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction along the actual coefficient projection is exact; its mapCochainComplexSingleFunctor isomorphism identifies the degree-zero restricted unit with the specified restriction of the degree-zero finite unit. Compose the augmentation with the inverse of this isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem integralReduction_twoTerm_resolution (n : ℕ) :
    let R := completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E Y D hl
    ∃ (Q : CochainComplex (Modules.{t, u} Y R) ℤ)
      (_ : flat.{t, u} Y R Q)
      (_ : ∀ k : ℤ, k ≠ -1 → k ≠ 0 → IsZero (Q.X k))
      (_ : Q.X (-1) ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
        ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
      (_ : Q.X 0 ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
        ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
      (epsilon : Q ⟶
        ((scalarReductionRestriction l E Y n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (scalarReductionTarget l E Y n) 0).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit (integralCoefficientSheaf l E Y n)))),
      QuasiIso epsilon
